heroHeadline: Xi Jinping Arrives in Washington for 3-Day State Visit as Taiwan Watches $14B Arms Package Fate; PLA Sorties Jump to 10 (9 Crossing), Highest Since Sept 18 Drill Window
heroSubtitle: Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Washington September 23, 2026 for a three-day state visit — his first White House trip in over a decade — with formal talks and a state dinner set for September 24; Taiwan's Defense Ministry said it would keep pressing to complete the $14 billion US arms package, paused since Trump and Xi's May Beijing summit, while US Sen. Pete Ricketts said Washington needed to keep signaling China 'they're not going to be allowed to take Taiwan by force.' Taiwan's major dailies reported September 22 that Washington had asked Taiwanese officials to reduce visits to the US ahead of the summit as the two governments prepared to establish a bilateral AI dialogue mechanism — fueling concern in Taipei that its profile could be minimized to smooth US-China talks. Hours before Xi's arrival, Taiwan's Army staged a live-fire media debut of its domestically built 'Cheetah' 105mm armored vehicle in Tainan, framed by AP's wire coverage as a display of self-reliant defense capability. Separately, Taiwan's MND recorded 10 PLA aircraft sorties (9 crossing the median line) and 12 PLAN/official ships in the 24 hours to September 23 — roughly double the 4-sortie counts of September 21 and 22 and the highest tally since the September 18 Jioupeng-drill window — coinciding with Xi's Washington arrival.
